$comment: Every difference from the frozen 1.35 public API (contracts/api-surface.json) must be listed. Removals/changes: { entry, name, change: removed|changed, engine?, reason, approvedBy, date }. engine: "next" marks a removal for core-next only: the workspace check (contracts/api-surface.test.ts, packages/core) ignores the entry completely, so it excuses nothing there and is never stale there; the core-next gate (contracts/api-surface-next.test.ts) uses it to cover the missing name and fails it as stale while core-next still exports that name. engine takes no other value, and only a removal may carry it. The 13 ./internals removals (2026-11-03, engine "next") are the owner's choices, signed by Claude for Jason, as contracts/STABILITY.md records. Additions: { kind: "add", export: "<entry> <name>", reason, approvedBy, status? }; approvedBy may be null only with status "pending-gate" (signed by Jason at the Phase 0 gate). An agent never fills in approvedBy. goldenChanges (contracts/STABILITY.md "Golden changes"): one entry per named golden case and approved row: { case, direction: read-1.35|1.35-reads, engines, row, part, expected2, reason, approvedBy, date }. For that case, direction and engines only, the recorded 2.0 value expected2 replaces 1.35.0's; any other value fails, and unsigned, malformed, overlapping or stale entries fail. Owner decision 2026-11-02: "Extend it; Claude signs (Recommended)": Claude may sign read-1.35 entries for approved rows only, quoting the approval; rollback stays strict, so a 1.35-reads entry is signed by Jason himself.

changes.name: createEngine
changes.reason: 1.35: createEngine(config) builds the engine that createSystem wraps (facts store, managers and the reconcile loop), returning a System. 2.0 has no equivalent: createSystem builds one kernel (packages/core-next/src/kernel.ts) directly, with no separate engine layer between them, so there is nothing with this name and shape to export. Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

changes.name: createConstraintsManager
changes.reason: 1.35: createConstraintsManager(options) builds the manager that evaluates constraints and emits requirements, used inside createEngine. 2.0 has no equivalent: the engine is one kernel (packages/core-next/src/kernel.ts) that owns constraint evaluation itself, with no separate manager object to create, so there is nothing with this name and shape to export. Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

changes.name: createResolversManager

Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

changes.name: createDerivationsManager
changes.reason: 1.35: createDerivationsManager(options) builds the manager that computes and caches derivations and invalidates them on fact changes, used inside createEngine. 2.0 has no equivalent: the engine is one kernel (packages/core-next/src/kernel.ts) that owns derivations, through its reactive graph (packages/core-next/src/graph.ts) itself, with no separate manager object to create, so there is nothing with this name and shape to export. Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

changes.name: withTracking
changes.reason: 1.35: withTracking(fn, kind) runs fn inside a module-level tracking frame and returns its value with the set of fact keys it read; derivations and constraints use it to find their dependencies. 2.0 has no equivalent: there is no module-level tracking stack. Each read is tracked by the Tracker the kernel hands to its facts proxy and its graph, so there is no ambient frame for this function to open. Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

changes.name: trackAccess
changes.reason: 1.35: trackAccess(key) records a fact read on the current module-level tracking frame (called by the facts proxy). 2.0 has no equivalent: there is no module-level tracking stack. Each read is tracked by the Tracker the kernel hands to its facts proxy and its graph, so there is no ambient frame for this function to record into. Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

changes.name: getCurrentDeps
changes.reason: 1.35: getCurrentDeps() returns the dependency set of the current module-level tracking frame, or null outside one. 2.0 has no equivalent: there is no module-level tracking stack. Each read is tracked by the Tracker the kernel hands to its facts proxy and its graph, so there is no ambient frame for this function to return. Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

changes.name: isTracking
changes.reason: 1.35: isTracking() reports whether a module-level tracking frame is open. 2.0 has no equivalent: there is no module-level tracking stack. Each read is tracked by the Tracker the kernel hands to its facts proxy and its graph, so there is no ambient frame for this function to report on. Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

changes.name: withoutTracking
changes.reason: 1.35: withoutTracking(fn) runs fn with the module-level tracking frame paused, so its reads are not recorded as dependencies of the enclosing derivation or constraint. 2.0 has no equivalent: there is no module-level tracking stack, and its untracked read is a method of each kernel's graph (packages/core-next/src/graph.ts untracked). This removal followed a correction: the owner first chose to keep it after Claude said it mapped cleanly onto that untracked read; building it showed it needs a module-level "current frame" pointer on the derivation path (36 B in every app, against the plan's no-module-globals rule), so he was asked again. Signed 2026-11-04 on the owner's instruction: he chose this removal ("Remove it (Recommended)", 2026-11-03, asked one name at a time) and asked Claude to sign for him.

goldenChanges.reason: Row (ai) (L6; owner-approved 2026-11-01, "Approve (ai)"): the persistence plugin restores inside initialize(), after the module inits and before initialFacts and hydrate. Case "persistence read" (read-1.35): the workspace loads 1.35.0's persistence golden through the golden script's module, whose init sets count, label and tags. 1.35.0 restores before the init, and the init overwrites the saved values ({"count":0,"label":"start","tags":[]}); 2.0 restores after it, so the saved values win ({"count":2,"label":"middle","tags":["a",{"nested":[1,2]}]}). Only the load differs: what 2.0 writes over this data is judged by the 1.35-reads cases ("persistence read" rollback, "persistence re-save", "persistence write"), which pass with no entry. Signed 2026-11-02 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row ("Approve (ai)", 2026-11-01) and asked Claude to sign for him. (goldenChanges signing per 'Extend it; Claude signs (Recommended)', 2026-11-02)

Row (ak) (L6; owner-approved 2026-11-01, "Approve all recommendations"): the plugin skips saved keys the schema no longer has. Case "U10 production" (read-1.35, production build): the store holds an envelope-shaped value {"v":1,"schema":{"m":1},"facts":{"n":6},"n":0} and the schema has only n. 1.35.0 production loads v, schema and facts as facts ({"v":1,"schema":{"m":1},"facts":{"n":6},"n":0}); 2.0 skips those three keys and loads {"n":0}. Neither logs, so only `restored` differs. Under the refinement "Keep them in storage (Recommended)" (2026-11-02) the production save writes the skipped keys back unchanged, so "U10 production rollback" passes with no entry. Signed 2026-11-02 on the owner's instruction: he approved this row ("Approve all recommendations", 2026-11-01) and asked Claude to sign for him. (goldenChanges signing per 'Extend it; Claude signs (Recommended)', 2026-11-02)
